## Question

Can a relational graph convolutional network (R-GCN) [@schlichtkrull2018]
rank held-out drug–disease treatment links in Hetionet [@himmelstein2017]
better than a common-neighbour baseline? This report describes the data, the
two models and their evaluation on held-out links over three random seeds.
The whole analysis runs on a CPU in a few minutes.

## Known treatments

```{python}
#| label: ctd
ctd = edges[edges["metaedge"] == "CtD"]
per_compound = ctd["source"].value_counts()
per_disease = ctd["target"].value_counts()
n_compounds = (nodes["kind"] == "Compound").sum()
n_diseases = (nodes["kind"] == "Disease").sum()
```

The model will predict the Compound–treats–Disease (CtD) edges. There are
`{python} f"{len(ctd)}"` of them, linking `{python} f"{per_compound.size}"` of
the `{python} f"{n_compounds:,}"` compounds and `{python} f"{per_disease.size}"`
of the `{python} f"{n_diseases}"` diseases. Most of these compounds
(`{python} f"{(per_compound == 1).sum()}"`) treat a single disease, while the
number of known treatments per disease ranges from 1 to
`{python} f"{per_disease.max()}"` (@fig-ctd). A model can therefore score well
by ranking the diseases that already have many treatments, so the evaluation
also uses negative pairs matched for this (@sec-split).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ctd
#| fig-cap: "Known treatments (CtD edges) per compound (left) and per disease (right), for the compounds and diseases that have at least one."
#| fig-alt: "Two histograms. Left: diseases treated per compound, from 1 to 19; about two thirds of the compounds treat one disease and the bars fall quickly after that. Right: known treatments per disease, from 1 to 68; the bars are spread over 1 to 16 treatments, with a tall bar at 1, and a sparse tail of about ten diseases between 21 and 68."
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.2))
left.hist(per_compound, bins=range(1, per_compound.max() + 2), color="#2a78d6")
left.set_xlabel("Diseases treated per compound")
left.set_ylabel("Compounds")
right.hist(per_disease, bins=range(1, per_disease.max() + 2), color="#eb6834")
right.set_xlabel("Known treatments per disease")
right.set_ylabel("Diseases")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Methods

```{python}
#| label: linkpred-setup
from scripts.linkpred import load_config, load_npz

config = load_config("config/config.yaml")
graph = load_npz("data/processed/graph.npz")
settings = config["model"]
seeds = config["seeds"]
n_target = len(graph["target"])
n_test = round(config["test_fraction"] * n_target)
n_val = round(config["val_fraction"] * n_target)
n_train = n_target - n_test - n_val
n_graph_nodes = len(graph["node_id"])
n_msg = len(graph["msg_src"])
n_relations = len(graph["relations"])
seed_list = ", ".join(str(s) for s in seeds[:-1]) + f" and {seeds[-1]}"
```

### Graph

The graph has the `{python} f"{n_graph_nodes:,}"` compounds, diseases and genes
of Hetionet and `{python} f"{n_msg:,}"` edges of `{python} f"{n_relations}"`
types: compound–gene (binds, upregulates, downregulates), disease–gene
(associates, upregulates, downregulates), compound–compound similarity and
disease–disease similarity (resembles). The training CtD pairs are added as one
more edge type. Every edge type is used in both directions, and each direction
is a relation of its own.

### Split and negative pairs {#sec-split}

For each of the seeds `{python} seed_list`, the `{python} f"{n_target}"` CtD
pairs are split at random into `{python} f"{n_train}"` training,
`{python} f"{n_val}"` validation and `{python} f"{n_test}"` test pairs. The
validation and test pairs are not in the graph. Negative pairs are
compound–disease pairs that Hetionet does not list as treatments (CtD) or as
palliative uses (CpD). Each test pair has two negatives. The random negative is
a compound and a disease drawn uniformly. The degree-matched negative takes its
compound from the compounds of the test pairs and its disease from their
diseases, so the negatives have the same numbers of known treatments as the
positives, and a score that only reflects these numbers is expected to reach
an AUROC close to 0.5.

### Models

The R-GCN [@schlichtkrull2018] learns a `{python} f"{settings['dim']}"`-dimensional
embedding for every node and passes it through `{python} f"{settings['layers']}"`
R-GCN layers with one weight matrix per relation. A DistMult decoder
[@yang2015] scores a compound–disease pair from the two node vectors. The model
is trained with binary cross-entropy against random negative pairs, using Adam
(learning rate `{python} f"{settings['lr']}"`, weight decay
`{python} f"{settings['weight_decay']}"`) and dropout of
`{python} f"{settings['dropout']}"`. In each epoch
`{python} f"{settings['supervision_fraction']:.0%}"` of the training CtD pairs
are scored and the others pass messages, so the model never scores a pair that
it also receives as an edge. Training stops after
`{python} f"{settings['max_epochs']}"` epochs, or earlier when the average
precision on the validation set has not improved for
`{python} f"{settings['patience']}"` epochs, and the model from the best epoch
is evaluated. The model is implemented with PyTorch Geometric [@fey2019] and
always runs with `{python} f"{config['threads']}"` threads, because the number of
threads can change the results of floating-point sums.

The baseline scores a pair by the number of common neighbours of the compound
and the disease in the same graph, without edge types: the genes linked to
both, the compounds similar to the compound that treat the disease, and the
diseases similar to the disease that the compound treats.

Both models are evaluated on the test pairs of each seed by the area under the
ROC curve (AUROC) and the average precision (AP), reported as mean ± standard
deviation over the three seeds. With one negative per positive, a random
ranking has an AUROC and an AP of about 0.5.

## Results

```{python}
#| label: results-setup
metrics = pd.read_csv("results/tables/metrics.tsv", sep="\t")
candidates = pd.read_csv("results/tables/candidates.tsv", sep="\t")
training = pd.concat(
    [pd.read_csv(f"results/rgcn/seed{s}_training.tsv", sep="\t").assign(seed=s) for s in seeds]
)


def metric(model, negatives, name):
    row = metrics[(metrics["model"] == model) & (metrics["negatives"] == negatives)].iloc[0]
    return row[f"{name}_mean"], row[f"{name}_std"]


def show(model, negatives, name="auroc"):
    mean, sd = metric(model, negatives, name)
    return f"{mean:.2f} ± {sd:.2f}"


def compare(negatives):
    higher = metric("R-GCN", negatives, "auroc")[0] > metric("Common neighbours", negatives, "auroc")[0]
    return "above" if higher else "below"


best = training[training["best"]]
```

With random negatives, the R-GCN reached an AUROC of
`{python} show("R-GCN", "random")` and the common-neighbour baseline
`{python} show("Common neighbours", "random")`, which places the R-GCN
`{python} compare("random")` the baseline (@tbl-metrics). With degree-matched
negatives, the AUROC of the R-GCN fell to `{python} show("R-GCN", "degree")`
and that of the baseline to `{python} show("Common neighbours", "degree")`,
which places the R-GCN `{python} compare("degree")` the baseline. The
R-GCN's ranking of the test pairs against random negatives therefore depends
largely on the numbers of known treatments of their compounds and diseases.
Average precision follows the same pattern.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-metrics
#| tbl-cap: "Test AUROC and average precision (mean ± SD over three seeds) of the R-GCN and the common-neighbour baseline, with random and degree-matched negatives."
table = metrics.assign(
    AUROC=[f"{m:.3f} ± {s:.3f}" for m, s in zip(metrics["auroc_mean"], metrics["auroc_std"])],
    AP=[f"{m:.3f} ± {s:.3f}" for m, s in zip(metrics["ap_mean"], metrics["ap_std"])],
    negatives=metrics["negatives"].map({"random": "random", "degree": "degree-matched"}),
)
(table[["model", "negatives", "AUROC", "AP"]]
 .rename(columns={"model": "Model", "negatives": "Negatives"})
 .style.hide(axis="index"))
```

Training stopped after `{python} f"{training.groupby('seed').size().min()}"` to
`{python} f"{training.groupby('seed').size().max()}"` epochs, with the best
validation AP at epochs
`{python} ", ".join(str(e) for e in best["epoch"][:-1]) + f" and {best['epoch'].iloc[-1]}"`
for the three seeds (@fig-training).

```{python}
#| label: fig-training
#| fig-cap: "Validation average precision of the R-GCN in each epoch, for each seed. The dot marks the epoch whose model was evaluated."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of validation average precision against training epoch, one line per seed; each line has a dot at its best epoch."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.2))
for (seed, run), color in zip(training.groupby("seed"), ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#3a9e5f"]):
    ax.plot(run["epoch"], run["val_ap"], color=color, label=f"seed {seed}")
    top = run[run["best"]]
    ax.plot(top["epoch"], top["val_ap"], "o", color=color)
ax.set_xlabel("Epoch")
ax.set_ylabel("Validation AP")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: candidates
treatments = per_disease.rename(index=dict(zip(nodes["id"], nodes["name"])))
candidate_treatments = treatments.reindex(candidates["disease"].unique()).fillna(0)
```

@tbl-candidates lists the `{python} f"{len(candidates)}"` compound–disease
pairs with the highest mean R-GCN probability over the three seeds, among the
pairs that Hetionet does not list as treatments or palliative uses. They involve
`{python} f"{candidates['compound'].nunique()}"` compounds and
`{python} f"{candidates['disease'].nunique()}"` diseases. These diseases have a
median of `{python} f"{candidate_treatments.median():.0f}"` known treatments,
against `{python} f"{per_disease.median():.0f}"` for all diseases with at least
one, which agrees with the drop in performance against degree-matched
negatives. The standard deviation of the probabilities across seeds ranges from
`{python} f"{candidates['sd'].min():.2f}"` to
`{python} f"{candidates['sd'].max():.2f}"`. The pairs are hypotheses from the
model and have not been checked against the literature.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-candidates
#| tbl-cap: "Compound–disease pairs with the highest R-GCN probability (mean and SD over three seeds) that are not known treatments or palliative uses in Hetionet."
(candidates.rename(columns={"rank": "Rank", "compound": "Compound", "disease": "Disease",
                             "probability": "Probability", "sd": "SD"})
 .style.hide(axis="index").format({"Probability": "{:.3f}", "SD": "{:.3f}"}))
```
